passages.text: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah. He came to Jonathan and asked, “What have I done? What is my iniquity? How have I sinned against your father, that he wants to take my life?”
passages.sermon:
David was in Naioth in Ramah.
Saul wanted to kill David.
David fled from Naioth in Ramah.
David went to Jonathan.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
David spoke to Jonathan.
David asked, “What have I done?”
David asked, “What is my guilt?”
David asked, “How have I sinned against your father?”
David said, “Why does your father want to kill me?”
passages.original: וַיִּבְרַ֣ח דָּוִ֔ד מִנֹּוִות בָּרָמָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֞א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן מֶ֤ה עָשִׂ֙יתִי֙ מֶֽה־ עֲוֺנִ֤י וּמֶֽה־ חַטָּאתִי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ כִּ֥י מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־ נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: “Far from it!” Jonathan replied. “You will not die. Indeed, my father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. So why would he hide this matter from me? This cannot be true!”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan said, “Far from it! You will not die.
My father is King Saul.
My father does nothing important or unimportant without telling me.
He always tells me everything he does.
Why would my father hide this thing from me?
This is not true.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֣וֹ חָלִילָה֮ לֹ֣א תָמוּת֒ הִנֵּ֡ה לוֹ־ עָשָׂה אָבִ֜י דָּבָ֣ר גָּד֗וֹל א֚וֹ דָּבָ֣ר קָטֹ֔ן וְלֹ֥א יִגְלֶ֖ה אֶת־ אָזְנִ֑י וּמַדּוּעַ֩ יַסְתִּ֨יר אָבִ֥י מִמֶּ֛נִּי אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אֵ֥ין זֹֽאת׃

passages.text: But David again vowed, “Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, ‘Jonathan must not know of this, or he will be grieved.’ As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, there is but a step between me and death.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Jonathan.
David made a vow.
David said, “Your father knows that I have found favor with you.
He said, ‘Jonathan must not know this.
If Jonathan knows, he will be sad.’
As surely as the LORD lives,
and as surely as you live,
there is only a step between me and death.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע ע֜וֹד דָּוִ֗ד וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יָדֹ֨עַ יָדַ֜ע אָבִ֗יךָ כִּֽי־ מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר אַל־ יֵֽדַע־ זֹ֥את יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן פֶּן־ יֵֽעָצֵ֑ב וְאוּלָ֗ם חַי־ יְהוָה֙ וְחֵ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ כִּ֣י כְפֶ֔שַׂע בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הַמָּֽוֶת׃

passages.text: Then Jonathan said to David, “Whatever you desire, I will do for you.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan was David’s close friend.
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan said, “Tell me what you want.”
Jonathan said, “I will do it for you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד מַה־ תֹּאמַ֥ר נַפְשְׁךָ֖ וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ לָּֽךְ׃פ

passages.text: So David told him, “Look, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I am supposed to dine with the king. Instead, let me go and hide in the field until the third evening from now.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Jonathan.
David said, “Tomorrow is the New Moon.”
David said, “I am supposed to eat with the king.”
David said, “Let me go instead.”
David said, “I will hide in the field.”
David said, “I will stay hidden until the third evening from now.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן הִֽנֵּה־ חֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ מָחָ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֛י יָשֹׁב־ אֵשֵׁ֥ב עִם־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וְשִׁלַּחְתַּ֙נִי֙ וְנִסְתַּרְתִּ֣י בַשָּׂדֶ֔ה עַ֖ד הָעֶ֥רֶב הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁית׃

passages.text: If your father misses me at all, tell him, ‘David urgently requested my permission to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because there is an annual sacrifice for his whole clan.’
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Jonathan.
David gave Jonathan instructions.
David said, "If your father notices I am absent, tell him this."
Say, 'David asked me for permission to go quickly to Bethlehem.'
Bethlehem is David's hometown.
David's family is holding an annual sacrifice there.
The whole clan will be at the sacrifice.
passages.original: אִם־ פָּקֹ֥ד יִפְקְדֵ֖נִי אָבִ֑יךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ נִשְׁאֹל֩ נִשְׁאַ֨ל מִמֶּ֤נִּי דָוִד֙ לָרוּץ֙ בֵּֽית־ לֶ֣חֶם עִיר֔וֹ כִּ֣י זֶ֧בַח הַיָּמִ֛ים שָׁ֖ם לְכָל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָֽה׃

passages.text: If he says, ‘Good,’ then your servant is safe, but if he is enraged, you will know he has evil intentions.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Jonathan.
David referred to Saul as Jonathan’s father.
David called himself Jonathan’s servant.
David gave Jonathan instructions.
David said, “If your father says, ‘Good,’ then I am safe.”
David said, “If your father becomes angry, you will know he has evil intentions.”
passages.original: אִם־ כֹּ֥ה יֹאמַ֛ר ט֖וֹב שָׁל֣וֹם לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְאִם־ חָרֹ֤ה יֶֽחֱרֶה֙ ל֔וֹ דַּ֕ע כִּֽי־ כָלְתָ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Therefore deal faithfully with your servant, for you have brought me into a covenant with you before the LORD. If there is iniquity in me, then kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Jonathan.
David was Jonathan’s friend.
David asked Jonathan to show kindness to him.
David said, “You brought me into a covenant with you before the LORD.”
David said, “If I have done wrong, you should kill me yourself.”
David asked, “Why should you bring me to your father?”
passages.original: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ חֶ֙סֶד֙ עַל־ עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ כִּ֚י בִּבְרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה הֵבֵ֥אתָ אֶֽת־ עַבְדְּךָ֖ עִמָּ֑ךְ וְאִם־ יֶשׁ־ בִּ֤י עָוֺן֙ הֲמִיתֵ֣נִי אַ֔תָּה וְעַד־ אָבִ֖יךָ לָמָּה־ זֶּ֥ה תְבִיאֵֽנִי׃פ

passages.text: “Never!” Jonathan replied. “If I ever found out that my father had evil intentions against you, would I not tell you?”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan said, “Never!”
Jonathan meant he would never let harm come to David without warning him.
Jonathan said, “If I ever knew my father planned evil against you, I would tell you.”
Jonathan promised to warn David if Saul wanted to harm him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן חָלִ֣ילָה לָּ֑ךְ כִּ֣י׀ אִם־ יָדֹ֣עַ אֵדַ֗ע כִּֽי־ כָלְתָ֨ה הָרָעָ֜ה מֵעִ֤ם אָבִי֙ לָב֣וֹא עָלֶ֔יךָ וְלֹ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then David asked Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Jonathan.
David asked a question.
David said, “Who will tell me?”
David wanted to know who would inform him.
David asked, “What if your father answers you harshly?”
David wanted to know who would tell him if Jonathan’s father responded with anger or harshness.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן מִ֖י יַגִּ֣יד לִ֑י א֛וֹ מַה־ יַּעַנְךָ֥ אָבִ֖יךָ קָשָֽׁה׃ס

passages.text: “Come,” he replied, “let us go out to the field.” So the two of them went out into the field, and Jonathan said, “By the LORD, the God of Israel, I will sound out my father by this time tomorrow or the next day. If he is favorable toward you, will I not send for you and tell you?
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
David was his close friend.
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan said, “Come with me.”
Jonathan told David to go out to the field with him.
Both Jonathan and David went out into the field.
Jonathan spoke to David in the field.
Jonathan said, “The LORD is the God of Israel.”
Jonathan said, “I will question my father Saul.”
Jonathan said, “I will do this by this time tomorrow or the next day.”
Jonathan said, “If my father is favorable toward you, I will send a message to you.”
Jonathan said, “I will tell you what my father says.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד לְכָ֖ה וְנֵצֵ֣א הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיֵּצְא֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃ס וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי־ אֶחְקֹ֣ר אֶת־ אָבִ֗י כָּעֵ֤ת׀ מָחָר֙ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֔ית וְהִנֵּה־ ט֖וֹב אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד וְלֹֽא־ אָז֙ אֶשְׁלַ֣ח אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְגָלִ֖יתִי אֶת־ אָזְנֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But if my father intends to bring evil on you, then may the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if I do not tell you and send you on your way in safety. May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
David was Jonathan’s close friend.
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan said, “If my father Saul plans to harm you, I will tell you.
If I do not warn you, may the LORD punish me.
May the LORD punish me very much if I fail to help you.
I will send you away in safety.
You will go in peace.
May the LORD be with you.
The LORD was with my father Saul.
May the LORD be with you in the same way.”
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ יַעֲשֶׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה לִֽיהוֹנָתָ֜ן וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֗יף כִּֽי־ יֵיטִ֨ב אֶל־ אָבִ֤י אֶת־ הָֽרָעָה֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ וְגָלִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ אָזְנֶ֔ךָ וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֖יךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וִיהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־ אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: And as long as I live, treat me with the LORD’s loving devotion, that I may not die, and do not ever cut off your loving devotion from my household—not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan was David’s close friend.
Jonathan said, “As long as I am alive, show me the LORD’s kindness.
Let me live.
Do not let me die.
Never stop showing your kindness to my family.
Keep your kindness to my household forever.
Do this even when the LORD destroys all of David’s enemies from the earth.”
passages.original: וְלֹ֖א אִם־ עוֹדֶ֣נִּי חָ֑י וְלֹֽא־ תַעֲשֶׂ֧ה עִמָּדִ֛י חֶ֥סֶד יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א אָמֽוּת׃ וְלֹֽא־ תַכְרִ֧ת אֶֽת־ חַסְדְּךָ֛ מֵעִ֥ם בֵּיתִ֖י עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם וְלֹ֗א בְּהַכְרִ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ אֹיְבֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אִ֕ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD hold David’s enemies accountable.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
David was a young man chosen by God to be king.
Jonathan made a covenant with David’s family.
Jonathan promised loyalty to David’s house.
Jonathan asked the LORD to punish David’s enemies.
Jonathan wanted the LORD to hold David’s enemies accountable.
passages.original: וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן עִם־ בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד וּבִקֵּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִיַּ֖ד אֹיְבֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃

passages.text: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his vow out of love for him, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan loved David deeply.
Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.
Jonathan asked David to make a vow again.
Jonathan did this because of his great love for David.
passages.original: וַיּ֤וֹסֶף יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ לְהַשְׁבִּ֣יעַ אֶת־ דָּוִ֔ד בְּאַהֲבָת֖וֹ אֹת֑וֹ כִּֽי־ אַהֲבַ֥ת נַפְשׁ֖וֹ אֲהֵבֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Then Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you will be missed if your seat is empty.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
David was Jonathan’s close friend.
Jonathan said, “Tomorrow is the New Moon.”
Jonathan said, “You will not be present.”
Jonathan said, “People will notice your seat is empty.”
Jonathan said, “You will be missed.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ ל֥וֹ יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן מָחָ֣ר חֹ֑דֶשׁ וְנִפְקַ֕דְתָּ כִּ֥י יִפָּקֵ֖ד מוֹשָׁבֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: When you have stayed three days, hurry down to the place you hid on the day this trouble began, and remain beside the stone Ezel.
passages.sermon:
David, you must wait for three days.
After three days, go down quickly.
Go to the place where you hid before.
You hid there on the day the trouble started.
Stay beside the stone called Ezel.
passages.original: וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ֙ תֵּרֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וּבָאתָ֙ אֶל־ הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ נִסְתַּ֥רְתָּ שָּׁ֖ם בְּי֣וֹם הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְיָ֣שַׁבְתָּ֔ אֵ֖צֶל הָאֶ֥בֶן הָאָֽזֶל׃

passages.text: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as if I were aiming at a target.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan was David’s friend.
Jonathan said, “I will shoot three arrows.”
I will shoot the arrows to the side of the stone.
I will shoot as if I am aiming at a target.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֕י שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הַחִצִּ֖ים צִדָּ֣ה אוֹרֶ֑ה לְשַֽׁלַּֽח־ לִ֖י לְמַטָּרָֽה׃

passages.text: Then I will send a boy and say, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ Now, if I expressly say to him, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,’ then come, because as surely as the LORD lives, it is safe for you and there is no danger.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan is David’s friend.
Jonathan will send a boy.
Jonathan will say to the boy, “Go. Find the arrows.”
If Jonathan says to the boy, “Look. The arrows are on this side of you. Bring them,” then David must come.
It is safe for David.
There is no danger for David.
The LORD lives.
Jonathan swears this by the LORD.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה֙ אֶשְׁלַ֣ח אֶת־ הַנַּ֔עַר לֵ֖ךְ מְצָ֣א אֶת־ הַחִצִּ֑ים אִם־ אָמֹר֩ אֹמַ֨ר לַנַּ֜עַר הִנֵּ֥ה הַחִצִּ֣ים׀ מִמְּךָ֣ וָהֵ֗נָּה קָחֶ֧נּוּ׀ וָבֹ֛אָה כִּֽי־ שָׁל֥וֹם לְךָ֛ וְאֵ֥ין דָּבָ֖ר חַי־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: But if I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, for the LORD has sent you away.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan is speaking to David.
\r\nJonathan gives David a secret signal.
\r\nJonathan says, “If I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’”
\r\nThis means the arrows are farther away from the young man.
\r\nIf Jonathan says this, David must leave.
\r\nDavid must go away.
\r\nThe LORD has sent David away.
passages.original: וְאִם־ כֹּ֤ה אֹמַר֙ לָעֶ֔לֶם הִנֵּ֥ה הַחִצִּ֖ים מִמְּךָ֣ וָהָ֑לְאָה לֵ֕ךְ כִּ֥י שִֽׁלַּחֲךָ֖ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And as for the matter you and I have discussed, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever.”
passages.sermon: Jonathan and David spoke together about an important matter.\r\nThe LORD stands as a witness between Jonathan and David.\r\nThe LORD will remain a witness between them forever.
passages.original: וְהַ֨דָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְנוּ אֲנִ֣י וָאָ֑תָּה הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינְךָ֖ עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃ס

passages.text: So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon had come, the king sat down to eat.
passages.sermon: David hid in the field.\r\nThe New Moon arrived.\r\nThe king sat down to eat.
passages.original: וַיִּסָּתֵ֥ר דָּוִ֖ד בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיְהִ֣י הַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ עַל הַלֶּ֖חֶם לֶאֱכֽוֹל׃

passages.text: He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan and beside Abner, but David’s place was empty.
passages.sermon:
King Saul sat down.
He sat in his usual place.
His usual place was by the wall.
Jonathan stood up.
Abner sat beside Saul.
David’s place was empty.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ עַל־ מ֨וֹשָׁב֜וֹ כְּפַ֣עַם׀ בְּפַ֗עַם אֶל־ מוֹשַׁב֙ הַקִּ֔יר וַיָּ֙קָם֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אַבְנֵ֖ר מִצַּ֣ד שָׁא֑וּל וַיִּפָּקֵ֖ד מְק֥וֹם דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: Saul said nothing that day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was not at the meal.
Saul noticed David’s absence.
Saul did not say anything that day.
Saul thought David was absent for a reason.
Saul believed David was ceremonially unclean.
Saul said to himself, “Something has happened to David.”
Saul thought, “David is not clean.”
Saul was sure David was unclean.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ דִבֶּ֥ר שָׁא֛וּל מְא֖וּמָה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא כִּ֤י אָמַר֙ מִקְרֶ֣ה ה֔וּא בִּלְתִּ֥י טָה֛וֹר ה֖וּא כִּֽי־ לֹ֥א טָהֽוֹר׃ס

passages.text: But on the day after the New Moon, the second day, David’s place was still empty, and Saul asked his son Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal either yesterday or today?”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
David was the son of Jesse.
The people gathered for a special meal at the New Moon.
On the second day after the New Moon, they met again for a meal.
David’s seat was empty.
Saul noticed that David was not there.
Saul spoke to Jonathan, his son.
Saul asked, “Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal?”
Saul said, “He was not here yesterday.”
Saul said, “He is not here today.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִֽמָּחֳרַ֤ת הַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וַיִּפָּקֵ֖ד מְק֣וֹם דָּוִ֑דס וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֔וֹ מַדּ֜וּעַ לֹא־ בָ֧א בֶן־ יִשַׁ֛י גַּם־ תְּמ֥וֹל גַּם־ הַיּ֖וֹם אֶל־ הַלָּֽחֶם׃

passages.text: Jonathan answered, “David urgently requested my permission to go to Bethlehem, saying, ‘Please let me go, because our clan is holding a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has told me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me go and see my brothers.’ That is why he did not come to the king’s table.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan spoke to Saul.
Jonathan answered Saul’s question.
David asked me for permission to go to Bethlehem.
David said, “Please let me go.”
David said, “Our family is offering a sacrifice in the city.”
David said, “My brother told me to be there.”
David said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please let me go.”
David said, “Let me go and see my brothers.”
That is why David did not come to the king’s table.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן אֶת־ שָׁא֑וּל נִשְׁאֹ֨ל נִשְׁאַ֥ל דָּוִ֛ד מֵעִמָּדִ֖י עַד־ בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃ וַיֹּ֡אמֶר שַׁלְּחֵ֣נִי נָ֡א כִּ֣י זֶבַח֩ מִשְׁפָּחָ֨ה לָ֜נוּ בָּעִ֗יר וְה֤וּא צִוָּֽה־ לִי֙ אָחִ֔י וְעַתָּ֗ה אִם־ מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אִמָּ֥לְטָה נָּ֖א וְאֶרְאֶ֣ה אֶת־ אֶחָ֑י עַל־ כֵּ֣ן לֹא־ בָ֔א אֶל־ שֻׁלְחַ֖ן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then Saul’s anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the disgrace of the mother who bore you?
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Saul became very angry with Jonathan.
Saul spoke to Jonathan.
Saul said, “You are the son of a perverse and rebellious woman.”
Saul said, “I know you have chosen the son of Jesse.”
The son of Jesse is David.
Saul said, “You have chosen David to your own shame.”
Saul said, “You have brought shame to your mother.”
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֤ף שָׁאוּל֙ בִּיה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בֶּֽן־ נַעֲוַ֖ת הַמַּרְדּ֑וּת הֲל֣וֹא יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־ בֹחֵ֤ר אַתָּה֙ לְבֶן־ יִשַׁ֔י לְבָ֨שְׁתְּךָ֔ וּלְבֹ֖שֶׁת עֶרְוַ֥ת אִמֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingship shall be established. Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must surely die!”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to Jonathan, his son.
Saul said, “The son of Jesse is David.”
David is still alive on this earth.
As long as David lives, you will not be secure.
Your kingship will not be secure either.
Now send for David.
Bring him to me.
He must die.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י כָל־ הַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֶּן־ יִשַׁי֙ חַ֣י עַל־ הָאֲדָמָ֔ה לֹ֥א תִכּ֖וֹן אַתָּ֣ה וּמַלְכוּתֶ֑ךָ וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁלַ֨ח וְקַ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ אֵלַ֔י כִּ֥י בֶן־ מָ֖וֶת הֽוּא׃ס

passages.text: “Why must he be put to death?” Jonathan replied. “What has he done?”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan spoke to his father Saul.
Jonathan asked Saul a question.
Jonathan said, “Why must he die?”
Jonathan also said, “What has he done?”
passages.original: וַיַּ֙עַן֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן אֶת־ שָׁא֖וּל אָבִ֑יו וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו לָ֥מָּה יוּמַ֖ת מֶ֥ה עָשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan to kill him; so Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul became very angry.
Saul picked up his spear.
Saul threw the spear at Jonathan.
Saul tried to kill Jonathan.
Jonathan saw what Saul did.
Jonathan understood his father’s intention.
Jonathan knew Saul was determined to kill David.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨טֶל שָׁא֧וּל אֶֽת־ הַחֲנִ֛ית עָלָ֖יו לְהַכֹּת֑וֹ וַיֵּ֙דַע֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן כִּֽי־ כָ֥לָה הִ֛יא מֵעִ֥ם אָבִ֖יו לְהָמִ֥ית אֶת־ דָּוִֽד׃ס

passages.text: Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger and did not eat any food that second day of the month, for he was grieved by his father’s shameful treatment of David.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Jonathan sat at the table with Saul.
Jonathan became very angry.
Jonathan stood up from the table.
Jonathan did not eat any food on the second day of the month.
Jonathan felt deep sorrow for David.
Jonathan’s father, Saul, had treated David with shame.
Jonathan grieved because of his father’s actions toward David.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧קָם יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן מֵעִ֥ם הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן בָּחֳרִי־ אָ֑ף וְלֹא־ אָכַ֞ל בְּיוֹם־ הַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ לֶ֔חֶם כִּ֤י נֶעְצַב֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד כִּ֥י הִכְלִמ֖וֹ אָבִֽיו׃ס

passages.text: In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for the appointment with David, and a small boy was with him.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Jonathan was a friend of David.
In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field.
Jonathan went to meet David at their appointed time.
A small boy went with Jonathan.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֵּצֵ֧א יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לְמוֹעֵ֣ד דָּוִ֑ד וְנַ֥עַר קָטֹ֖ן עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He said to the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.” And as the boy ran, Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan spoke to a young boy who was with him.
Jonathan said to the boy, “Run.”
Jonathan told the boy, “Find the arrows I shoot.”
The boy began to run.
Jonathan shot an arrow.
Jonathan shot the arrow beyond the boy.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְנַעֲר֔וֹ רֻ֗ץ מְצָ֥א נָא֙ אֶת־ הַ֣חִצִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מוֹרֶ֑ה הַנַּ֣עַר רָ֔ץ וְהֽוּא־ יָרָ֥ה הַחֵ֖צִי לְהַעֲבִרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the boy reached the place where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen, Jonathan called to him, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?”
passages.sermon:
A small boy went with Jonathan to the field.
Jonathan shot an arrow.
The boy ran to find the arrow.
The boy reached the place where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen.
Jonathan called out to the boy.
Jonathan said, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א הַנַּ֙עַר֙ עַד־ מְק֣וֹם הַחֵ֔צִי אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָרָ֖ה יְהוֹנָתָ֑ן וַיִּקְרָ֨א יְהוֹנָתָ֜ן אַחֲרֵ֤י הַנַּ֙עַר֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הֲל֥וֹא הַחֵ֖צִי מִמְּךָ֥ וָהָֽלְאָה׃

passages.text: Then Jonathan cried out, “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” So the boy picked up the arrow and returned to his master.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan spoke to his servant boy.
Jonathan shouted to the boy.
He said, “Hurry!”
He said, “Make haste!”
He said, “Do not delay!”
The boy listened to Jonathan.
The boy picked up the arrow.
The boy returned to Jonathan, his master.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַנַּ֔עַר מְהֵרָ֥ה ח֖וּשָׁה אַֽל־ תַּעֲמֹ֑ד וַיְלַקֵּ֞ט נַ֤עַר יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ אֶת־ הַחֵצִי וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־ אֲדֹנָֽיו׃

passages.text: But the boy did not know anything; only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
David was Jonathan’s close friend.
Jonathan and David made a secret arrangement.
The boy did not know anything about this arrangement.
Only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.
passages.original: וְהַנַּ֖עַר לֹֽא־ יָדַ֣ע מְא֑וּמָה אַ֤ךְ יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ וְדָוִ֔ד יָדְע֖וּ אֶת־ הַדָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: Then Jonathan gave his equipment to the boy and said, “Go, take it back to the city.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of King Saul.
Jonathan had a servant boy with him.
Jonathan gave his equipment to the boy.
Jonathan said to the boy, “Go.”
Jonathan told the boy, “Take the equipment back to the city.”
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהֽוֹנָתָן֙ אֶת־ כֵּלָ֔יו אֶל־ הַנַּ֖עַר אֲשֶׁר־ ל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ לֵ֖ךְ הָבֵ֥יא הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: When the young man had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone, fell facedown, and bowed three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together—though David wept more.
passages.sermon:
David was hiding near the stone in the south.
The young man left.
David stood up.
David fell facedown to the ground.
David bowed three times.
David and Jonathan were close friends.
David and Jonathan kissed each other.
David and Jonathan wept together.
David wept more than Jonathan.
passages.original: הַנַּעַר֮ בָּא֒ וְדָוִ֗ד קָ֚ם מֵאֵ֣צֶל הַנֶּ֔גֶב וַיִּפֹּ֨ל לְאַפָּ֥יו אַ֛רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ פְּעָמִ֑ים וַֽיִּשְּׁק֣וּ׀ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֗הוּ וַיִּבְכּוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֔הוּ עַד־ דָּוִ֖ד הִגְדִּֽיל׃

passages.text: And Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘May the LORD be a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and mine forever.’ ” Then David got up and departed, and Jonathan went back into the city.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan said, “Go in peace.”
Jonathan and David had made a promise together.
They both swore this promise in the name of the LORD.
They said, “The LORD will be a witness between you and me.”
They said, “The LORD will be a witness between my descendants and your descendants forever.”
David stood up.
David left.
Jonathan returned to the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן לְדָוִ֖ד לֵ֣ךְ לְשָׁל֑וֹם אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨עְנוּ שְׁנֵ֜ינוּ אֲנַ֗חְנוּ בְּשֵׁ֤ם יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֞ה יִֽהְיֶ֣ה׀ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֗ךָ וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעִ֛י וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃פ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ וִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן בָּ֥א הָעִֽיר׃
